drafted_from: tool:give-a-stripe-customer-a-credit's own row (its words and input schema) and the take-payments function it runs, whose tests use made-up Stripe replies; read it before relying on it
start_here: Say to your AI: "Give my Stripe customer a credit off their next invoice", with {"customer": "cus_test_sample0301", "amount_cents": 1500, "currency": "usd", "description": "Referral reward for a friend's first lesson", "idempotency_key": "referral-reward:friend-0302", "secret_name": "bakery-stripe-secret-key-test"}. It runs tool:give-a-stripe-customer-a-credit and answers {"balance_transaction": "cbtxn_test_sample0303", "customer": "cus_test_sample0301", "credit_cents": 1500, "currency": "usd", "ending_balance": -1500}.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input, asks Stripe with your own key, and answers; it keeps no row.
instructions: 1. Prove it first with a Stripe test-mode key: say to your AI "Give my Stripe customer a credit off their next invoice" with a test customer and your test key's vault name in secret_name.
2. The AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:give-a-stripe-customer-a-credit and that input (the worked example shows one).
3. Read what comes back: the balance transaction Stripe booked and the customer's ending balance; asking again with the same idempotency_key books nothing more.
4. Only then give it the live key's name, from the workflow that decides the reward, never by hand.
